key_insight: BRDFusion combines physically-based inverse rendering with generative modeling to better reconstruct and re-render urban scenes from video. The key idea is to keep the realism and controllability of physics while using generation to reduce artifacts and improve visual quality.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of inverse rendering urban scenes from captured videos: physics-based methods are often artifact-prone, while generative approaches look realistic but lack consistency and control.
method: Uses a unified framework that fuses two complementary models: one for inverse rendering and one for forward rendering.
Leverages physical lighting and material modeling to preserve scene consistency and controllability.
Injects generative priors to improve realism and reduce reconstruction/rendering artifacts in complex urban environments.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work offers a practical path toward more believable and controllable scene reconstruction from real video. It is especially relevant for applications like content creation, digital twins, and autonomous driving simulation.
visual_elements: A split pipeline diagram showing physics-based inverse rendering and generative forward rendering merging into one system
Before/after image panels comparing artifact-heavy reconstructions vs BRDFusion outputs
An urban scene visualization with labeled lighting, materials, geometry, and camera paths
A trade-off chart contrasting realism, consistency, and controllability across methods
paper_title: BRDFusion: Physics Meets Generation for Urban Scene Inverse Rendering
paper_authors: Yi-Ruei Liu, Jie-Ying Lee, Zheng-Hui Huang, Yu-Lun Liu, Chih-Hao Lin
